narration_timeline.text: A giraffe can reach food high above the ground, but how does it take a bite?
narration_timeline.scene: Giraffe at supervised feeding center; clearly captive setting.

narration_timeline.text: Its long neck brings leaves and feeders closer while its feet remain planted, even when the food is presented in a supervised zoo setting.
narration_timeline.scene: Giraffes in two different zoos showing full body and neck.

narration_timeline.text: It moves its head toward the greenery, working its mouth near the food with small, deliberate motions instead of one quick snap.
narration_timeline.scene: Zoo giraffe near foliage; two independent shots require action review.

narration_timeline.text: The lips and tongue help guide vegetation inward; reaching a branch is only the beginning.
narration_timeline.scene: Zoo giraffe muzzle in view; avoid claiming unshown bite.

narration_timeline.text: These animals were filmed in different managed settings, not as one wild herd.
narration_timeline.scene: Giraffes in separate zoo group footage.

narration_timeline.text: In open habitat, that reach brings leaves within range for the next mouthful.
narration_timeline.scene: Giraffe visibly reaching vegetation in natural-looking landscape.
